disclaimer: Educational demo dataset for the NTPU Sustainability and ESG Data Analytics course. Claims are condensed, paraphrased illustrations modelled on the style and themes of public sustainability reports; figures are rounded or approximate and page numbers are indicative. Pillar scores are AI-assisted audit judgements produced with the GreenWash-Screener methodology, not official ratings. GreenTech Corp is fictional. Always verify against the original reports before drawing conclusions about any real company.

claims.claim_text: In 2023, Scope 1 and Scope 2 (market-based) GHG emissions totalled approximately 11.9 million tCO2e; point-of-use abatement systems were installed on all new fab process tools to destroy fluorinated process gases, and the GHG inventory was verified under ISO 14064-1 with third-party assurance.
claims.audit_justification: Absolute tCO2e, market-based Scope 2 and PFC abatement address the most material Scope 1 lever for a foundry. Third-party verification is cited. The statement is backward-looking, so it does not by itself show the reduction trajectory.

claims.claim_text: TSMC targets net-zero emissions by 2050, with interim goals to return to 2020 emission levels by 2025 and to reduce emissions 25% below 2020 levels by 2030.
claims.audit_justification: Base year (2020) and interim milestones (2025, 2030) satisfy most IFRS S2 target requirements. The covered scopes and the planned use of carbon credits are not specified in the claim, and no SBTi validation is cited, which keeps it in the grey zone.

claims.claim_text: Renewable energy accounted for about 9% of total electricity consumption in 2023; TSMC aims for 60% renewable electricity company-wide by 2030 and 100% by 2040 (RE100), supported by long-term power purchase agreements including large-scale offshore wind contracts.
claims.audit_justification: Current share, interim 2030 milestone and long-term RE100 date form a credible trajectory backed by PPAs (additional capacity). Transparent disclosure of the low current share reduces greenwashing risk.

claims.claim_text: Process water recycling across fabs reached roughly 87%, and TSMC targets a 30% reduction in unit water consumption by 2030 compared with the 2010 baseline, while scaling reclaimed-water plants in Southern Taiwan Science Park.
claims.audit_justification: Quantified recycling rate and an intensity target with baseline year. Absolute withdrawal in water-stressed regions (required by SASB) is not shown in the claim, so scope coverage is partial.

claims.claim_text: TSMC requires its key suppliers to set carbon reduction targets and launched a supplier sustainability academy; supplier emissions are on a decreasing trajectory.
claims.audit_justification: Addresses the material Scope 3 supply chain but provides no tCO2e, no share of suppliers with targets and no base year. 'Decreasing trajectory' is unverifiable as stated.

claims.claim_text: As a green manufacturing leader, TSMC is committed to building a low-carbon, sustainable future for the semiconductor industry.
claims.audit_justification: Generic leadership language ('green manufacturing leader', 'sustainable future') with no metric, scope or verification. Under Directive 2024/825 such generic claims require recognised excellent performance to be substantiated.

claims.claim_text: Scope 3 emissions are disclosed for all relevant GHG Protocol categories, with Category 1 purchased goods and services as the largest source; the inventory is reported in line with TCFD and SASB TC-SC-110a.1.
claims.audit_justification: Full-scope disclosure with category-level breakdown and standard mapping. No Scope 3 reduction target is attached to this disclosure.

claims.claim_text: We matched 100% of the electricity used in offices and data centers under our operational control with renewable energy (market-based), through a mix of renewable energy certificates and power purchase agreements.
claims.audit_justification: Quantified and boundary-specific, but operational electricity is a small share of a fabless company's footprint and the REC/PPA split is not given, so additionality is unclear.

claims.claim_text: Our science-based targets validated by SBTi: reduce absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions 50% by FY2030 from a FY2023 base year, and ensure suppliers covering 67% of Scope 3 purchased goods emissions set science-based targets by FY2026.
claims.matched_standard: SBTi Corporate Net-Zero Standard / IFRS S2 para 36
claims.audit_justification: Absolute target, base year, near-term horizon, Scope 3 supplier engagement target and third-party SBTi validation: a textbook legit target disclosure.

claims.claim_text: Our Scope 3 footprint is dominated by Category 1 purchased goods and services and Category 11 use of sold products; all relevant categories are quantified in tCO2e and disclosed in our CDP climate response.
claims.audit_justification: Correctly identifies the material categories for a fabless GPU designer and quantifies them. No Category 11 reduction target despite it being a key driver.

claims.claim_text: Our latest GPU platform delivers up to 25x better energy efficiency for large-language-model inference than the prior generation, making accelerated computing the most sustainable path for AI.
claims.audit_justification: Efficiency ratio is a vendor benchmark ('up to') without absolute use-phase emissions. Rebound effects mean Category 11 absolute emissions can still grow; 'most sustainable path' is an unsubstantiated superlative.

claims.claim_text: Scope 1, Scope 2 and selected Scope 3 GHG emissions received limited assurance from an independent third party in accordance with ISAE 3410.
claims.audit_justification: Clear assurance standard and level. 'Selected' Scope 3 categories means part of the material footprint is unassured.

claims.claim_text: Accelerated computing is sustainable computing, and AI will help the world solve climate change.
claims.audit_justification: A sweeping, unquantified marketing slogan that ignores the growing absolute energy demand of AI data centers. No metric, boundary or verification.

claims.claim_text: Intel reached about 99% renewable electricity in the U.S., Europe, Israel and Malaysia, and about 93% globally in 2023 (market-based).
claims.audit_justification: Specific, geography-level renewable shares with market-based accounting. Location-based impact and instrument mix are not shown in the claim.

claims.claim_text: Intel commits to net-zero Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions across global operations by 2040, with interim milestones of 100% renewable electricity and a 10% absolute reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030 from a 2019 baseline.
claims.audit_justification: Long-term target with base year, interim 2030 milestones and an absolute metric. Scope 3 is excluded from this commitment (covered separately).

claims.claim_text: We are investing approximately $300 million in facility conservation and abatement to cut PFC and other high-GWP process emissions, targeting 4,000 GWh of cumulative energy savings by 2030.
claims.audit_justification: CAPEX-backed action plan targeting the material Scope 1 source (fluorinated gases) with a quantified 2030 objective - strong evidence of resourcing as required by IFRS S2.

claims.claim_text: Intel targets net-positive water by 2030 and restored or returned billions of gallons in 2023, with water data reviewed by an independent third party.
claims.audit_justification: Time-bound target with third-party review. 'Net positive' relies on restoration projects, so absolute withdrawals in water-stressed regions should be disclosed alongside.

claims.claim_text: Intel aims to achieve net-zero upstream Scope 3 emissions by 2050 in partnership with suppliers and customers.
claims.audit_justification: Addresses the material Scope 3 but only as a distant aspiration with no interim milestone, no base-year value and no validation in the claim itself.

claims.claim_text: GHG emissions, energy and water data were independently verified with limited assurance under ISAE 3000/3410 and reported against GRI 305, SASB TC-SC-110a.1 and TCFD.
claims.audit_justification: Explicit assurance standard, level and indicator mapping across GRI, SASB and TCFD.

claims.claim_text: Intel is a sustainability leader whose innovation enables a greener world for everyone.
claims.audit_justification: Unsubstantiated self-declared leadership and 'greener world' wording without any metric or scope.

claims.claim_text: The DX (device) division aims to achieve net zero by 2030 and the company targets net zero by 2050, transitioning all global sites to renewable energy (RE100) by 2050.
claims.audit_justification: Dates are given but the claim lacks a base year, the role of carbon credits and validation. The semiconductor (DS) division, the main emitter, is on the slowest timeline.

claims.claim_text: Renewable energy reached about 31% of total electricity in 2023, with 100% renewable electricity at sites in the United States, Europe and China.
claims.audit_justification: Quantified share with regional breakdown. Korean fabs, the largest electricity consumers, are not covered by the 100% figure.

claims.claim_text: We plan to invest about KRW 7 trillion by 2030 in environmental initiatives, including process-gas abatement and water recycling.
claims.audit_justification: CAPEX commitment supports credibility, but expected tCO2e outcomes and allocation per initiative are not disclosed.

claims.claim_text: Our eco-conscious Galaxy devices use recycled materials and plastic-free packaging, helping protect the planet.
claims.audit_justification: 'Eco-conscious' and 'protect the planet' are generic claims; packaging is marginal versus product use-phase and manufacturing emissions. No recycled-content share is given.

claims.claim_text: Scope 1 and 2 (market-based) emissions are verified by an independent third party, and Scope 3 emissions are disclosed for all 15 categories, with Category 11 use of sold products as the largest source.
claims.audit_justification: Complete scope coverage with third-party verification of operational emissions.

claims.claim_text: The semiconductor business will reduce process gas emissions through next-generation regenerative catalytic systems that treat fluorinated gases at fabs.
claims.audit_justification: Targets the right material source (PFCs) but without destruction efficiency, coverage percentage or deadline.

claims.claim_text: Samsung is building a greener tomorrow with innovative, sustainable technologies for everyone.
claims.audit_justification: Purely aspirational marketing language with no metric, boundary or evidence.

claims.claim_text: Hon Hai targets a 42% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030 from a 2020 base year, aligned with the SBTi 1.5°C pathway, and net-zero emissions by 2050.
claims.matched_standard: SBTi Corporate Net-Zero Standard / IFRS S2 para 36
claims.audit_justification: Base year, absolute interim target and 1.5°C alignment. Scope 3 is not covered by this target although it dominates an EMS footprint.

claims.claim_text: Renewable electricity increased in 2023 through solar installations on factory rooftops and T-REC purchases.
claims.audit_justification: Directionally positive, but the claim gives no share or MWh, and unbundled T-RECs may lack additionality.

claims.claim_text: Our electric vehicle platform will contribute to a green, low-carbon mobility revolution.
claims.audit_justification: Future-performance marketing claim without lifecycle analysis, avoided-emission methodology or verification.

claims.claim_text: We require key suppliers to sign a carbon reduction commitment; suppliers representing about 80% of procurement spend have signed.
claims.audit_justification: Engagement metric is quantified but signatures are not reduction outcomes; no tCO2e or supplier target quality is disclosed.

claims.claim_text: Scope 3 emissions include Category 1 purchased goods and Category 11 use of sold products; other categories are still under evaluation.
claims.audit_justification: Partial Scope 3 boundary without quantified figures in the claim and without justification for excluded categories.

claims.claim_text: Our campuses host 100,000 trees and plastic-free canteens, demonstrating our commitment to environmental protection.
claims.matched_standard: TerraChoice Sin of Irrelevance / SASB TC-ES materiality
claims.audit_justification: Marginal campus initiatives presented as environmental commitment while material manufacturing and supply-chain emissions are not mentioned (cherry-picking).

claims.claim_text: Scope 1 and 2 GHG data were verified under ISO 14064-1 by an independent body, and the report is prepared with reference to GRI and TCFD.
claims.audit_justification: Third-party verification of operational emissions; 'with reference to' GRI is weaker than 'in accordance with'.

claims.claim_text: ASE has committed to setting SBTi near-term targets and aims for net-zero by 2050, with an interim goal to reduce carbon intensity 25% by 2025 compared with 2016.
claims.matched_standard: SBTi Net-Zero Standard / IFRS S2 para 33-36
claims.audit_justification: Base year and interim milestone exist, but the interim target is intensity-based and SBTi status is 'committed', not 'validated'.

claims.claim_text: Water reclamation plants at our Kaohsiung sites recycled several million cubic meters of water in 2023, raising the site water recycling rate above 20%.
claims.audit_justification: Quantified volume and rate for a water-stressed region; no forward target or group-wide figure in the claim.

claims.claim_text: Several ASE buildings have obtained LEED Platinum certification, reflecting our green factory philosophy.
claims.audit_justification: Certification is third-party, but building labels are a narrow slice of the footprint and no emissions outcome is quantified.

claims.claim_text: Renewable energy accounted for a growing share of electricity in 2023, and ASE aims to reach RE100 by 2050.
claims.audit_justification: Long-term RE100 date without a 2030 milestone in the claim; current share not stated precisely.

claims.claim_text: Scope 1, 2 and 3 GHG inventories were verified with limited assurance under ISO 14064-1 by an independent third party and reported according to GRI 305 and TCFD.
claims.audit_justification: Full-scope inventory with stated assurance level and standard mapping.

claims.claim_text: We strive to be a low-carbon pioneer in semiconductor packaging, creating harmony between technology and nature.
claims.audit_justification: Aspirational, vague wording ('pioneer', 'harmony with nature') without metrics or verification.

claims.claim_text: GreenTech is a 100% eco-friendly chipmaker with green DNA in every wafer.
claims.audit_justification: Textbook generic environmental claim banned under Directive 2024/825 unless excellent performance is demonstrated. Zero metrics, scope or verification.

claims.claim_text: We aspire to become carbon neutral by 2050 through eco-friendly innovation and a holistic sustainability journey.
claims.audit_justification: Distant aspiration with no base year, no interim target, no scope and no plan - fails IFRS S2 target disclosure requirements.

claims.claim_text: Our headquarters cafeteria is now powered by rooftop solar panels and is fully plastic-free.
claims.matched_standard: SASB TC-SC-110a.1 / TerraChoice Sin of Irrelevance
claims.audit_justification: Marginal HQ initiative while fab energy and PFC process emissions - the material sources - are omitted.

claims.claim_text: We planted 10,000 trees in 2023, offsetting our carbon footprint and making our operations climate neutral.
claims.audit_justification: Offset-based neutrality claim, explicitly banned for products under Directive 2024/825; 10,000 trees sequester a negligible amount versus a fab's emissions and permanence is unverified.

claims.claim_text: Our products are designed with the planet in mind and comply with all international environmental standards.
claims.audit_justification: Blanket compliance claim with no named standard, indicator or certificate - the TerraChoice 'Sin of No Proof'.

claims.claim_text: Energy consumption at our flagship office decreased 12% thanks to LED lighting upgrades.
claims.audit_justification: A real number, but for a single office; manufacturing energy is not disclosed, so the claim is immaterial.

claims.claim_text: GreenTech purchased renewable energy certificates equal to 100% of its electricity, making us a renewable-powered leader.
claims.audit_justification: Unbundled certificates without additionality or location-based disclosure; 'leader' is self-declared.

claims.claim_text: Scope 3 emissions are outside our control and therefore not reported.
claims.audit_justification: Explicit exclusion of Scope 3, which IFRS S2 makes mandatory after the first reporting year and which SBTi requires to be targeted when above 40% of emissions.
